VERIFY: The weekly refresh workflow opens one PR with the regenerated baseline and a medium-shard drift table; first refresh run id recorded
GATE: First baseline accepted only if its summed time is within 10% of the median summed time of the source runs and it covers at least 95% of currently collected fast-tier ids
GUARDRAIL: The refresh workflow only opens PRs (contents and pull-requests write); it never pushes to develop, merges, or edits the baseline outside a PR; API calls bounded and logged
VERIFY: The baseline stores per-test p50 normalized by each source run's runner-speed factor, plus the source runs' factors; refresh rejects source runs missing a calibration value

description: A reviewable reference that cannot drift silently. A script (unit-tested, reusing tests/duration_policy.py helpers including _junit_nodeid normalization) builds a schema-versioned JSON of per-test p50 seconds from the last ~20 merged-PR fast-job junit artifacts (same configuration as the PR gate: coverage on, -n auto). A weekly scheduled workflow regenerates it and opens a PR; that PR also reports medium-shard drift between tests/fixtures/medium_shard_durations.json and measured shard junit, recommending a refresh when skew exceeds 20%. A PR that intentionally slows tests updates the baseline itself with the same script and states why in its body. Do not route refresh through nightly workflows (mostly red in the 2026-10-10..24 window).
